original_question: How do graph-complex symmetries Ṗ=O→r(γ)(P) act on the Ikeda–Izawa Poisson σ-model, whose Feynman path-integral expansion encodes the Kontsevich star-product? In addition, does that σ-model possess symmetries that do not originate from graph cocycles γ in ker d?
target_in_paper: The draft is closest to the paper’s unlabelled open problem in its final quantum-aspects discussion: to understand how the universal infinitesimal Poisson symmetries produced from graph-complex cocycles act at the level of the Ikeda–Izawa Poisson sigma-model underlying Kontsevich’s deformation quantization, and whether that sigma-model has additional symmetries not encoded by cocycles in the graph complex.
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the main objects tied together in the paper’s quantum-aspects question: (i) universal graph-complex symmetries of Poisson brackets written as Pdot = O_r(γ)(P), (ii) the Ikeda–Izawa Poisson sigma-model, and (iii) the fact that this sigma-model is related to the Feynman expansion of the Kontsevich star-product. It also correctly captures the second half of the paper’s question, namely whether there are sigma-model symmetries not coming from graph cocycles.
missing_details: The paper works with Poisson bi-vectors P on smooth finite-dimensional affine manifolds (over R); the draft does not state this ambient geometric setting.
γ should be identified as a d-cocycle in Kontsevich’s unoriented graph complex; the draft says 'graph cocycles' but does not specify the complex or the differential d.
The map O_r should be described as the graph-orientation morphism sending a graph cocycle γ to a universal infinitesimal deformation Q(P) = O_r(γ)(P) of the Poisson bi-vector.
The infinitesimal nature of the symmetry is implicit in the draft but should be made explicit as the deformation P ↦ P + ε O_r(γ)(P) + O(ε^2).
The draft does not say that the induced deformation is universal/natural with respect to the Poisson manifold, which is part of the paper’s setup for graph-generated Poisson symmetries.

The phrase 'act on the Ikeda–Izawa Poisson sigma-model' is too vague unless one specifies that the question concerns realization at the level of the sigma-model/path integral/correlation functions that produce Kontsevich’s graph expansion.

The paper’s context is specifically the Poisson sigma-model used in deformation quantization; the draft should make explicit that the relevant observables are the correlation functions whose perturbative expansion yields Kontsevich’s star-product.

The second clause should be sharpened to ask whether every relevant infinitesimal symmetry of that sigma-model comes from some γ in ker d, or whether there exist additional sigma-model symmetries outside the graph-complex construction.
refined_question: Let P be a Poisson bi-vector on a smooth finite-dimensional affine manifold, let γ ∈ ker d be a cocycle in Kontsevich’s unoriented graph complex, and let Q(P) = O_r(γ)(P) be the universal infinitesimal Poisson symmetry obtained from γ by the orientation morphism. In the Ikeda–Izawa (equivalently, Cattaneo–Felder) Poisson sigma-model whose perturbative correlation functions reproduce Kontsevich’s star-product for P, how is the infinitesimal deformation P ↦ P + εQ(P) + O(ε^2) realized as a symmetry of the sigma-model and of its path-integral expansion? Conversely, does that Poisson sigma-model admit infinitesimal symmetries relevant to deformation quantization that are not induced by any graph-complex cocycle γ ∈ ker d?
justification: The draft does not match the paper’s combinatorial or PDE-type open problems; it matches the paper’s quantum-aspects question. The abstract already says that one of the paper’s themes is the 'quantum aspects' of graph-generated Poisson symmetries. The introduction provides the two pieces of context needed to decode the notation: graph cocycles generate universal infinitesimal Poisson symmetries, and the Ikeda–Izawa/Cattaneo–Felder Poisson sigma-model gives the Feynman-graph interpretation of Kontsevich’s star-product. The final quantum-aspects discussion then asks how those graph-generated symmetries are seen on the sigma-model side and whether the sigma-model has further symmetries not originating from graph cocycles. The refined question keeps exactly that scope and does not broaden it beyond the sigma-model/deformation-quantization setting.
